title: Integrated circuit breakthrough
before: Circuits were assembled from discrete components, limiting density and reliability.
problem: Complex electronics needed many components connected reliably in tiny spaces.
change: Independent work associated with Jack Kilby (Texas Instruments) and Robert Noyce (Fairchild) produced early integrated circuits around 1958–1959; public demonstrations and commercialization followed.
whyItMattered: Putting multiple devices on one chip unlocked exponential growth in capability later summarized by Moore's Law discussions.
enabled: Microprocessors, dense memory, affordable personal computing.
concreteExample: A modern microcontroller integrates CPU, memory, and peripherals on one die—an IC concept scaled massively.
caveat: Attribution involves overlapping inventions and patents; avoid simplistic single-inventor 'first' slogans.
